# KConfig codec fixtures

Fixture corpus for `internal/plasma`'s KConfig INI codec. Three families, one
assertion each, plus a fuzz corpus seeded from all three.

## `canonical/` — Family A

Generated by the **real `/usr/bin/kwriteconfig6`** (kconfig 6.29) against a
throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`, so every byte is KDE's own canonical output.

Assertion: `Write(Parse(raw))` is **byte-identical** to `raw`. This is the
codec's acceptance bar — it proves the escape table, both sort comparators and
the blank-line layout match the implementation the codec has to interoperate
with.

| Fixture | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `escapes.ini` | Every row of the escape table in all three contexts: backslash, LF, TAB, CR, `=`, `[`, `]`, edge spaces, interior spaces, `#`, never-escaped punctuation, UTF-8 |
| `control_bytes.ini` | C0 controls and DEL in group, key and value context |
| `dollar_groups.ini` | The `\x24` last-segment rule and all four of its negative cases |
| `flags_locale.ini` | `[$e]` / `[$i]` / `[$d]`, `[de]` / `[de_DE]` / `[fr]`, and a group-level `[$i]` with its propagated entry flags |
| `high_bytes.ini` | Valid UTF-8 raw; stray bytes and overlong forms escaped per byte |
| `root_group.ini` | Root-group entries written first with no header line |
| `real_shapes.ini` | The payload shapes that actually occur: tab-joined shortcut lists, JSON blobs with unescaped brackets, `file://` URLs, dotted timestamps, quoted activity strings, nested `[Colors:Header][Inactive]` and `[Libinput][…][…][…]` headers |

## `noncanonical/` — Family B

Hand-written inputs that are deliberately **not** canonical.

Assertion: **one-pass normalisation, then idempotence** —
`Write(Parse(raw))` == `Write(Parse(Write(Parse(raw))))`, and the first pass is
expected to differ from the input.

`codec_fixture_test.go` also pins what each normalisation actually produces, so
a change of heart shows up as a test diff rather than as a surprise in a live
config.

Three of them exist specifically to pin behaviour that was settled by
**differentially probing the real `kwriteconfig6` / `kreadconfig6`** rather than
by reading the C++ (the pinned forms below were confirmed against kconfig 6.29
in a throwaway `XDG_CONFIG_HOME`):

| Fixture | Covers |
| --- | --- |
| `group_trim.ini` | The two-mode group header decode — a bracket segment with **no** backslash is the name verbatim, one **with** a backslash is trimmed of raw edge whitespace first — plus the 0x1D segment split. KDE's own writer merges two of these groups into one; we keep them apart |
| `immutable_tombstone.ini` | The propagated group `[$i]` is the one flag `d` does **not** suppress: inside `[G][$i]`, every tombstone comes back as `[$di]` |
| `lone_backslash.ini` | A lone trailing backslash is **dropped**, not kept, in key, value and group context. Both of these files' normalised forms are byte-identical to `kwriteconfig6`'s own rewrite |

## `real/` — Family C

**Scrubbed** copies of the maintainer's actual KDE files. They were written by
KDE, so they are canonical and carry the Family A byte-identical bar as well.

These are committed to a public repository. Scrubbing is a hard requirement, and
`TestCodec_FamilyC_IsScrubbed` fails the build if a refresh forgets it:

| Identifier | Replacement |
| --- | --- |
| Every UUID (desktop, activity, monitor/output) | `00000000-0000-4000-8000-0000000000NN`, numbered in sorted order so group ordering is preserved |
| The per-install application shortcut token | `DEADBEEFDEADBEEFDEADBEEFDEADBEEF` |
| Application reverse-DNS id and friendly name | `com.example.Synthetic` |
| Absolute home paths | `/home/testuser` |
| Personal cloud folder names | generic XDG folder names |
| Input device names | `Synthetic Pointer Device` / `Synthetic Keyboard Device` |
| NAS mount path | `/mnt/storage` |
| Hostnames, IP addresses, MAC addresses | removed entirely |

The scrubbing preserves **structure** — bracket nesting, escape sequences, key
and group ordering — which is all these tests exercise. Where a substitution
could change sort order (UUID group headers, the token key name), the
replacement was chosen to keep the original relative order.

## Refreshing the corpus

Regenerate Family A on a host with `kwriteconfig6`, always against a throwaway
`XDG_CONFIG_HOME` — **never** the real `~/.config`. Re-scrub Family C before
committing and let `TestCodec_FamilyC_IsScrubbed` confirm it.
